title: Claim a slice and surface claimed / in-work items in list

sections.heading: Why
sections.body:
slicer tracks in-work with the `started` status, and `slicer list` already shows
started items (it hides only done and retired). What is missing is a *claim*: there
is no record of who or which worktree is working a slice, so nothing survives across
the per-branch, git-tracked state (the S105 duplicate-work incident — see S113), and
the default `list` does not make in-work work stand out, since a started item just
sorts among open items by effective score. An agent scanning `list` cannot tell what
is actively being worked, or by whom, before picking something up.

sections.heading: Files
sections.body:
- `src/slicer/model.py` and `src/slicer/ops.py` — the claim record (owner/worktree
  and when) and the commands that set and clear it.
- `src/slicer/cli.py` (`cmd_list` / `_item_rows`) — surface claimed and in-work rows
  distinctly and name the owner; keep `--json` a superset.
- `src/slicer/vcs.py` — only if the claim reads worktree/branch identity (read-only).
- list tests, and `README.md` / `docs/getting-started.md` for the claim workflow.

sections.heading: Failing tests
sections.body:
1. Claiming a slice records an owner (and time) and `slicer list` shows the item as
   claimed with that owner; `--json` carries the claim fields.
2. `slicer list` surfaces in-work (started) and claimed items distinctly from plain
   open items — grouped or marked — by default.
3. Releasing or finishing a claim clears it; a done slice is never shown as claimed.

sections.heading: Implement
sections.body:
Add a lightweight claim to a slice/item — who (a configurable identity, e.g. the git
user or the worktree) and when — set when work starts and cleared when it finishes or
is released. Surface claimed and in-work items distinctly in `slicer list` (group or
mark them, name the owner), with `--json` a superset that carries the claim fields.
Coordinate the claim representation with S113 so one record powers both the
cross-branch warning and the list display. Keep render/`log.jsonl` determinism intact.

Product decision to settle first, not to infer from the backlog: whether a claim is a
new status, a field on the item, or a separate (possibly non-git) record — and how it
interacts with the per-branch state that made S113 necessary. Agree this with the
project before building; it may split into a claim-record slice and a list-display
slice.

sections.heading: Check
sections.body:
The cases above pass. `slicer list` (text and `--json`) shows claimed / in-work items
distinctly and names the owner; a released or finished claim no longer shows.
`slicer check` and the suite pass.

sections.heading: Git
sections.body:
One commit, or a small series, once the representation is settled. Coordinate with
S113. Do not tag or push.
